newsitem.title: USA: Motorola sees wireless users doubling.
newsitem.headline: Motorola sees wireless users doubling.

text.p: Motorola Inc projects that the number of users of wireless devices worldwide will double in the next five years from about 225 million in 1995 to about 550 million in the year 2000, a top executive said.

Merle Gilmore, executive vice president as well as president and general manager of Motorola's Land Mobile Products Group, also said that the phenomenal growth in use of various wireless devices in the past five years from 70 million users in 1990 to 225 million last year, still leaves about 98 percent of the world's population as an untapped market opportunity.
Industrywide subscriber growth covered use of pagers, cellular phones and two-way radios.
He spoke at Montgomery Securities' Investment Conference here.
This growth of the wireless market will benefit Motorola, since 60 percent of Motorola's revenues are from wireless communications, he said.
Gilmore said he sees a big opportunity arising for two-way radio because it offers instant, on-the-spot conferencing and two-way communications.
Asked about the problem of price erosion in wireless handsets, which hurt Motorola's most recent quarterly earnings, Gilmore said pricing pressure in the handset market "will be an ongoing issue."
New competition in the handset market, brought on by current cheap prices of component parts, has made it a cut-throat business with pricing as the weapon.
